newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT shareholders approve restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: NTT shareholders approve restructuring plan.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's restructuring plan was approved by shareholders with a big round of applause on Friday, although some questioned NTT's strategy of spinning off profitable businesses from the parent.
NTT's senior executive vice president Yutaka Hayashi told the firm's annual shareholders' meeting that the benefit of restructuring NTT under a holding company would be large.
"We will develop new businesses (and) advance into international services making the most of our comprehensive power," he said, stressing the benefit of NTT's new units belonging to one group.
NTT will be restructured into three units under a holding company in June 1999. The holding company will take over NTT's current shareholders.

Although shareholders approved the plan, which was greeted with a burst of applause, some complained that NTT's strategy of spinning off profitable businesses, such as data communications and cellular phone services, is detrimental to profitability at the parent company.
NTT president Junichiro Miyazu said the multimedia business, such as digital networks and open computer networks, will help to push up profits at the parent company.
About 1,700 shareholders attended Friday's meeting, which ended after a relatively quiet session lasting less than two hours.
